gotchas.procedure_section: Schedules K-1 - Debt Basis vs Stock Basis Distribution Trap
gotchas.title: Distributions exceed STOCK basis; debt basis is positive
gotchas.trap: Look at total basis (stock $338,640 + debt $120,000) and treat the $360,000 distribution as tax-free.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Distributions reduce stock basis only. Stock basis before distributions $338,640 -> $21,360 is gain from the sale of stock (sec. 1368(b)(2)) - Form 8949 Part II box F, long-term; Form 7203 attached. Debt basis absorbs only the nondeductible expenses/charitable items (debt basis EOY $114,900).

gotchas.title: IL PTE tax on the K-1-P
gotchas.trap: Add the $16,073 PTE tax paid by the corporation to Schedule A line 5a as state income tax, and/or ignore the IL credit.
gotchas.correct_treatment: The PTE tax was deducted by the corporation (ordinary income is already net of it) - it is not the shareholder's itemized tax. Claim the $16,073 credit on the IL-1040 (Schedule K-1-P); no IL subtraction.
gotchas.impact: Sch A overstated / IL refund understated

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule A - itemizing SALT (refund of taxes itemized in the prior year)
gotchas.title: 1099-G $2,100 IL refund
gotchas.trap: Report the $2,100 on Schedule 1 line 1 because she itemized in 2024.
gotchas.correct_treatment: 2024 SALT was capped at $10,000 with $31,000 paid; without the overpayment she would still have been capped -> no tax benefit -> $0 taxable (tax benefit rule, Rev. Rul. 2019-11). Keep the worksheet.

gotchas.title: MAGI above $500,000
gotchas.trap: Deduct the full $40,000 cap (or $32,350 paid), and include the 01/15/2026 IL estimate.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Cap = 40,000 - 30% x ($552,750 - 500,000) = $24,175. Only IL payments made in 2025 count (withholding + 3 estimates); total paid $32,350 -> limited to $24,175.

gotchas.procedure_section: Schedule A - Charitable Contributions (DAF vs GoFundMe; noncash clothing)
gotchas.title: Three kinds of 'donations'
gotchas.trap: Deduct GoFundMe $1,500 and value clothing at 3x cost per the procedure ($1,800) or at cost ($600).
gotchas.correct_treatment: DAF $25,000 deductible in 2025 (public charity, written acknowledgment). GoFundMe for a colleague's family is a gift to individuals - not deductible. Used clothing is limited to FMV (thrift value) ~$150 - the procedure's 3x-cost rule conflicts with sec. 170 (FMV of used clothing cannot exceed its cost) and is not followed.
gotchas.impact: Sch A line 11/12 overstated $3,150 if wrong

gotchas.procedure_section: Review - Hand-off / estimated payments (organizer vs. confirmation)
gotchas.title: Organizer says 4 x $15,000 federal estimates
gotchas.trap: Enter $60,000 on line 26 from the organizer -> understated balance due, IRS math-error notice, no 2210.
gotchas.correct_treatment: IRS account shows 3 payments ($45,000; Q3 missed). Line 26 = $45,000. 90% of 2025 tax < 110% of 2024 tax -> required annual payment $120,006; Form 2210 regular method penalty $779 (line 38).

gotchas.title: Medical practice S corp with $612k of W-2 wages
gotchas.trap: Claim 20% x $310,000 = $62,000 because the W-2 wage limit is met.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Health is an SSTB; taxable income before QBI is above $247,300 (single) -> applicable percentage 0% -> QBI deduction $0.

gotchas.title: Excess-distribution gain and K-1 income on Form 8960
gotchas.trap: Include the K-1 ordinary income and/or the $21,360 excess-distribution gain in NII.
gotchas.correct_treatment: K-1 income is nonpassive trade/business income (material participation) - not NII. The excess-distribution gain is treated as gain on S-corp stock and removed on line 5c to the extent attributable to the active business (sec. 1411(c)(4), Prop. Reg. 1.1411-7; all corporate assets used in the practice). NII = interest + dividends $4,890 -> NIIT $186.

gotchas.procedure_section: Scan - duplicate documents (draft vs final K-1)
gotchas.title: DRAFT K-1 received before the final
gotchas.trap: Autoflow both K-1s, or use the draft ($326,100 box 1 - before the PTE tax deduction).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Use only the FINAL K-1 (box 1 $310,000); bookmark the draft as superseded.

software_exceptions.title: S-corp distribution above STOCK basis (debt basis does not cover distributions)
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: If beginning basis is keyed as one blended figure ($28,000 stock + $120,000 shareholder loan = $148,000), Axcess tests the $360,000 distribution against $148,000 + $310,640 of income = $458,640 and treats it as fully tax-free. No capital gain is generated.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Income/Deductions > S Corporation Passthrough > Basis Limitation section: beginning STOCK basis $28,000 on the stock-basis line; shareholder loan $120,000 entered only in the separate DEBT-basis lines. Recalculate - $21,360 excess distribution flows to Form 8949 box F (LT; held since 2016). Form 7203 attached.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: ProConnect requires 'Stock basis at beginning of year' to produce Form 7203 (missing entry raises diagnostic ref 56844). If the preparer types the blended $148,000 there, the same tax-free result occurs.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: S Corp Info (1120S K-1) > Shareholder's Basis (7203): Stock basis at beginning of year = 28,000; Debt basis at beginning of tax year = 120,000 (Shareholder Loan section). 7203 generates because a distribution was received; the $21,360 gain flows to Schedule D.
software_exceptions.proconnect_reference: Intuit help: 'How to complete Form 7203 and resolve diagnostic 56844 in ProConnect Tax'
software_exceptions.efile_impact: None (Form 7203 required attachment when a distribution is received)
software_exceptions.procedure_section: Schedules K-1 - Debt Basis vs Stock Basis Distribution Trap
software_exceptions.notes: Workbook tab 12 formula corrected to apply distributions before losses (Reg. 1.1367-1(f)); see Corrections Log.

software_exceptions.title: Form 2210 - organizer says 4 estimates, only 3 were paid
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: Axcess computes the underpayment penalty from whatever estimates are keyed. Keying the organizer (4 x $15,000) shows no penalty; nothing compares the organizer to the IRS account transcript.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: General > Payments: enter federal estimates by actual date paid (04/15, 06/16, 01/15/2026 = $15,000 each; Q3 $0). Penalty section: regular method, no waiver; 110% prior-year safe harbor applies (2024 AGI $508,300 > $150,000). Penalty $779 on line 38.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - ProConnect uses the estimate amounts/dates entered; no transcript check.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Payments, Penalties & Extensions: enter each 2025 federal estimate with its actual date paid (leave Q3 blank); let the Form 2210 penalty compute (do not check 'suppress penalty').
software_exceptions.proconnect_reference: Screen name per current release - verify
software_exceptions.notes: Workbook tab 8 (corrected) shows required annual payment $120,006 vs payments $101,360 -> NOT met.

software_exceptions.title: SSTB flag missing from K-1 statement - QBI deduction would be ~$62,000
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: The K-1's Section 199A statement reports QBI, W-2 wages and UBIA but the corporation did not check the SSTB box. Axcess applies the W-2 wage limit only and allows a ~$62,000 QBI deduction (20% x $310,000; wage limit $120,000 and taxable-income limit $91,273 do not bind).
software_exceptions.axcess_override: S Corporation Passthrough > Section 199A: check 'Specified service trade or business'. With taxable income before QBI of $479,825 (> $247,300) the SSTB is fully phased out - QBI deduction $0.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - ProConnect relies on the SSTB indicator entered from the K-1 statement.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: S Corp Info (1120S K-1) > Qualified Business Income (199A): 'Specified service trade or business' = Yes.
software_exceptions.notes: Pediatric medical practice is a health SSTB under 199A(d)(2).

software_exceptions.title: NIIT - excess-distribution gain on active S-corp stock (Form 8960 line 5c)
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: The $21,360 Schedule D gain is treated as net investment income automatically (+$812 NIIT). Axcess cannot know the corporation's assets are 100% used in a nonpassive trade or business.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Form 8960 input: line 5c adjustment (disposition of partnership interest or S-corp stock) = (21,360), supported by a Reg. 1.1411-7 (proposed, may be relied on) statement. NIIT falls to $186.
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - capital gain flows into NII.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Net Investment Income Tax (8960) screen: 'Adjustment for disposition of partnership interest or S corporation stock' = -21,360; attach statement.
software_exceptions.proconnect_reference: Field label per current release - verify
software_exceptions.notes: Position flagged for signer (NIIT $812 higher if not taken).

software_exceptions.title: State refund (1099-G $2,100) - tax benefit rule when PY SALT was capped
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: For a new client or when the 2024 Schedule A detail did not proforma, Axcess's state-refund worksheet has no PY SALT/cap data and includes the full $2,100 on Schedule 1 line 1.
software_exceptions.axcess_diagnostic: Informational: state and local refund worksheet requires prior-year itemized deduction information
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Income > State and local refund worksheet: enter 2024 state and local taxes paid ($31,000), SALT limitation $10,000, 2024 itemized total; worksheet computes $0 taxable (Rev. Rul. 2019-11).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same - the taxable-refund worksheet needs prior-year itemized and SALT-limit data; otherwise the full refund is taxable.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Income > State and local tax refunds: complete the prior-year Schedule A / SALT limitation fields so the worksheet limits the taxable amount to $0.
software_exceptions.proconnect_reference: Verify field names in current release
software_exceptions.procedure_section: Schedule A - refunds of taxes itemized in a prior year

software_exceptions.title: Illinois PTE tax - federal Schedule A vs IL credit
software_exceptions.axcess_default_behavior: If the K-1's 'state taxes paid by entity' footnote is keyed as an estimated state payment, Axcess both itemizes it (federal) and credits it (IL) - double benefit. The tax was already deducted inside K-1 box 1.
software_exceptions.axcess_override: Do not enter the PTE tax on the federal Taxes worksheet. Enter $16,073 only on the IL K-1-P passthrough credit input (IL Schedule IL-E / PTE credit). IL exemption and property-tax credit are disallowed (AGI > $250,000).
software_exceptions.proconnect_default_behavior: Same risk if entered under state estimated payments.
software_exceptions.proconnect_fix: Illinois return > Pass-through entity credits: enter the IL K-1-P PTE tax credit $16,073; nothing on federal Taxes (Schedule A).
software_exceptions.efile_impact: IL return e-filed with K-1-P information
